fix: 'internode(s)' is mapped to stem; it should map to shoot axis internode, which exists in PO (the pipeline already uses PO_0005005 as a 'towards' target, e.g. A01743).

target: lanceolate or ovate-lanceolate (second alternative is the compound shape ovate-lanceolate, not ovate)
fix: Joined shape words like 'X-Y' (ovate-lanceolate, ovate-oblong) are cut at the hyphen and only the first part is kept as the value. Read the whole word as one value: the Y shape tending toward X (or Y with an X qualifier), never as X alone.
reason: The flora says the bracts are lanceolate or ovate-lanceolate. An ovate-lanceolate bract is narrow, not ovate.
'Calyx … 5-lobed' means five calyx lobes. The count goes on calyx lobe, as the counted-parts pattern says.
The inflorescence is shorter than the internodes. The comparison target is shoot axis internode.

fix: For 'glandular-puberulent', the glandular part of the hairs is dropped. It could be added as a second value, but the alternatives themselves are read correctly.
reason: The buds are puberulent or densely pubescent: two alternatives at the level of the taxon, both pilosity values.

target: hairy only on the midvein and margins of the abaxial leaflet surface (place restriction: midvein, margin)
fix: In 'abaxially hairy only at X and Y', the 'only at X and Y' part limits where the hairs are. It should become a part restriction (midvein, margin), or the bearer should be the abaxial midvein and the margin. Otherwise the whole underside is wrongly said to be hairy.
reason: The flora restricts the hairs to the midvein and margins. The annotation says the whole abaxial surface is pubescent.
The leaf blade is glabrous on its abaxial side.
'Septum absent, rarely rudimentary': absence is the usual state. The rare exception does not make the negation wrong.
The base of the blade is cuneate.
'2–7-céphales' means corymbs of 2–7 heads. The count is on capitulum inside a corymb.

fix: The 'ca.' before 3 mm is not kept as an approximate qualifier. That is a small loss.
reason: In '5-8 × ca. 3 mm' the second number is the width of the spikelet.
The stems range from decumbent to erect, a range of positions.
'Hairless above' on the leaves means the adaxial surface of the blade is glabrous.

Both surfaces of the blade are tomentose when young. The 'young' stage slot is set.
The moss leaf cells are densely papillose. The bearer is the cell, inside the leaf.

fix: In 'A shorter than B', the comparison is put on the parent organ (stamen) and not on the named part A. The subject before 'shorter/longer than' should be the bearer.
reason: The flora says the filament is shorter than the anther. A stamen contains its anther, so it cannot be shorter than it.

target: leaf apex (PO_0020137) acumen / drip tip, not the leaf lamina
fix: In 'apex acuminate with tip N mm', the number measures the acumen (tip). It should go on the apex or acumen, not on the blade. The blade length is given earlier (4-10 cm).
reason: 10-20 mm is the length of the pointed tip. The blade is 4-10 cm long.
The monocarps (fruitlets) are red at maturity. Fruit color red with the 'mature' slot is right.
The lamina is ± asymmetric, with the approximate qualifier.
The blades are ± lanceolate, with the approximate qualifier.

target: pedicel of the female (pistillate) flower, length to 1.5 cm in fruit
fix: Under a heading like 'Female flowers: pedicels …', the whole slot (pistillate flower) is lost. Phrases under sex-specific headings should carry the female or male flower as the whole.
reason: The stage slot 'in fruit' is right. But only the female pedicels lengthen, so 'pedicels to 1.5 cm' is false for the male flowers.

fix: 'Nearly' is not kept as an approximate qualifier. It should be, as with '±'.
reason: The upper stipules are nearly distinct, which means free. The 'upper' context and the 'free' value are right.
'Stems scapiform … ebracteate' means no bracts on the scape. Bract with negated 'present' is right.
The branchlets range in color from greenish to gray.
The leaflets are glabrous above, on the adaxial surface.
'Thorns & Spines: Absent' means thorns are absent.

fix: 'Upper part' may belong only to the color clause ('light brown'), with 'densely hairy' said of the whole stipe and rachis. Either way the restricted statement stays true.
reason: The upper part of the stipe is densely hairy. That is true whether the hairs cover the whole stipe or only its upper part.
Anisophyllous means the leaves of a pair differ in size, so the size value 'unequal' is right.

target: possibly beaked (FLOPO:0991028) on the fruit apex
fix: 'Short-tipped' on a legume usually means a short beak (the persistent base of the style) rather than a minute mucro. The rule that maps 'short-tipped' to mucronulate should check the bearer. Also, the apex shape should go on the fruit apex.
reason: Mucronulate means a minute abrupt point. The flora's 'short-tipped' pod could equally mean shortly beaked.
